archetypes.notes: The envelope floor is 0.1 C, not the 0.5 C proposed in the v1.2 review pack. The pack attributed a cooling magnitude near 2 C to yao2023a; retrieval at implementation established that the paper reports no such figure and instead measures 0.1-0.6 C by day. Blue-space cooling varies with time of day, season and location; at night blue spaces may exacerbate the urban heat island, and sensible cooling can be offset by increased water-vapour content.

archetypes.notes: THIS ARCHETYPE MUST NEVER BE INTERPOLATED WITH large_water_body BY AREA. sources.finding: Review of 51 green-blue infrastructure types across 202 publications: allotments and city farms are among the least-studied categories, with insufficient data to quantify their cooling.

archetypes.notes: Derived, not retrieved: bounded below dense_tree_canopy on the ziter2019 canopy-cover inflection and the colter2019 sparse-canopy finding, and given the same envelope as established_park with a lower evidence rating. resolved.notes: THIS ARCHETYPE MUST NEVER BE INTERPOLATED WITH large_water_body BY AREA. curation_reasons.A1: Deliberately sited single tree addressing a defined local heat problem; distinct from an isolated existing tree, which the document disqualifies.
curation_reasons.A2: Overlapping canopies produce a continuous shaded microclimate distinct from the same trees dispersed; different soil-volume and spacing requirements.
curation_reasons.A3: Document distinguishes a grove from a cluster as a composed collective structure forming a defined shaded room for occupation.
curation_reasons.A4: Distinct and near-universal physical detail, but the document calls it a minimum planting provision rather than a preferred NbS typology.
curation_reasons.A5: Substantially greater rooting volume gives different tree longevity, water storage and failure behaviour than a conventional pit.
curation_reasons.A6: Engineered soil-and-stone medium under paving is a distinct substrate with its own specification, usable-volume limits and installation risks.
curation_reasons.A7: Load-bearing frame over uncompacted soil is a different construction and maintenance system from structural soil, with different cost and utility constraints.
curation_reasons.A8: Deliberate hydrological connection to adjacent runoff makes it a distinct system; the document calls it more accurately an NbS than a conventional pit.
curation_reasons.A9: Engineered filter media, storage zones and underdrainage give clogging, sediment and maintenance behaviour genuinely different from a basic stormwater pit.
curation_reasons.A11: Canonical continuous below-ground rooting volume serving a sequence of trees; also functions as a stormwater conveyance and storage structure.
curation_reasons.A12: Visible unpaved connected soil strip; surface permeability and soil exposure differ from a buried trench under pavement.
curation_reasons.A13: Several vegetation layers give higher evapotranspiration, habitat and maintenance complexity than the tree-only strip in A12.
curation_reasons.A14: Planted island interrupting a large paved or trafficked surface; distinct form and size-dependent performance.
curation_reasons.B1: Physically distinct, but is effectively the umbrella of B2–B4 and the document says a decorative bed is not automatically NbS.
curation_reasons.B2: Shrub layer gives ground-level shading and road/building buffering where trees are impossible; distinct visibility and safety constraints.
curation_reasons.B3: Canonical perennial planting system; distinct vegetation structure, seasonal cover and maintenance regime from shrub or groundcover beds.
curation_reasons.B4: Continuous low soil cover replacing gravel, bare soil or mown turf; distinct surface-temperature and soil-moisture behaviour.
curation_reasons.B6: Meadow community with low-frequency cutting is a distinct vegetation and management system, not an ornamental perennial bed.
curation_reasons.B7: Shallow ground-connected planted depression storing and infiltrating runoff; the document calls it a genuine small-scale NbS.
curation_reasons.B8: Linear conveyance function, check dams and longitudinal space requirements distinguish it from the discrete rain-garden basin.
curation_reasons.B9: Hydraulically connected but undepressed and without engineered filter layers or underdrainage; different siting constraints from bioretention.
curation_reasons.B10: Engineered media, storage volume and overflow give different failure and maintenance behaviour from a simple rain garden.
curation_reasons.B11: Explicitly distinguished from an ordinary decorative container by hydraulic connection; enables retrofit where ground infiltration is impossible.
curation_reasons.B12: Connected large planters create a continuous vegetated edge with shared rooting volume where excavation is impossible; distinct from single stormwater planters.
curation_reasons.C1: Shallow substrate, stress-tolerant vegetation and low structural load form a distinct roof system with limited street-level cooling.
curation_reasons.C2: Intermediate substrate depth supports wider vegetation and water storage with different structural and irrigation demands from extensive roofs.
curation_reasons.C3: Deep growing medium supporting lawns, shrubs and trees; distinct structural load, drainage and maintenance regime.
curation_reasons.C5: Varied substrate depths, mineral materials and microhabitats form a physically different roof build-up from a standardised planting mat.
curation_reasons.C6: Locally characteristic nutrient-poor substrate and open heterogeneous habitat is a distinct substrate specification, though it overlaps biodiverse roofs.
curation_reasons.C8: Canonical vegetated roof with dedicated water storage feeding plants; integrates stormwater, evapotranspiration and habitat in one build-up.
curation_reasons.C11: Coordinated PV-and-vegetation build-up with panel spacing, substrate and access designed together; the NbS-qualifying form of the solar-green roof.
curation_reasons.C13: Edible planting with raised beds, deeper substrate and nutrient and irrigation management is a distinct roof system from ornamental green roofs.
curation_reasons.C14: Distinct in scale and management intensity from a productive roof, but the document says it is not automatically NbS unless ecological conditions are met.
curation_reasons.C15: Meadow community needs more varied substrate and moisture than a sedum roof and a mowing regime; distinct build-up and management.
curation_reasons.C16: Wetland vegetation with controlled standing water on a roof is a specialised hydraulic and waterproofing system with strong evaporative cooling.
curation_reasons.C17: Multiple trees on a roof demand soil depth, anchoring and wind assessment beyond an intensive roof, with different failure behaviour.
curation_reasons.D1: Self-clinging plants on the wall surface with no support frame; lowest technical complexity and distinct facade-maintenance implications.
curation_reasons.D2: Canonical ground-rooted system on a separate support with an air gap; the gap changes facade protection and ventilation behaviour.
curation_reasons.D5: Rooting in planters at multiple levels creates irrigation dependency and failure sensitivity genuinely different from ground-rooted facades.
curation_reasons.D6: Trailing growth downward from elevated planters is a distinct physical arrangement with its own container, drainage and access constraints.
curation_reasons.D7: Canonical living wall: modular panels fixed to a support structure with integrated irrigation and drainage; rapid coverage, pump-failure risk.
curation_reasons.D8: Substrate buffering of water and nutrients gives different weight, drying and failure behaviour, but it overlaps the modular wall in D7.
curation_reasons.D9: Soil-free inert medium with fully engineered nutrient delivery; dependence on mechanical systems and skilled maintenance is distinct from substrate walls.
curation_reasons.D11: Freestanding vertical vegetated structure not part of a facade; used for shade, privacy, wind and glare control.
curation_reasons.D12: Acoustic structure combined with vegetation; distinct construction, siting along transport corridors and soil-connection requirements.
curation_reasons.D13: Load-retaining structure with integrated planting cells, terraces or pockets; vegetation stabilises surfaces and reduces exposed mineral heating.
curation_reasons.E1: Canonical overhead frame carrying climbers above an occupied space; delivers shade before or instead of mature tree canopy.
curation_reasons.E3: Linear repeated-bay covered route giving continuous pedestrian shade along a corridor; distinct geometry from a discrete pergola.
curation_reasons.E6: Canonical vegetated shelter providing shaded thermal refuge at stops, schools, markets and interchanges; qualifies where vegetation is real and managed.
curation_reasons.2.2: Canonical integrated linear canopy system: continuous connected tree-soil rows (A10-A13) producing a continuous shaded corridor. Distinct form, distinct cooling behaviour.
curation_reasons.2.5: The canonical comprehensive street-scale system: vegetation, engineered soils, bioretention and public-realm improvement coordinated across the right-of-way.
curation_reasons.2.9: Canonical linear vegetated strip within the carriageway cross-section: de-sealed, plantable, often bioretentive. Distinct retrofittable form with its own cooling behaviour.
curation_reasons.2.13: Genuinely distinct linear system: vegetation replaces ballast and asphalt within the rail alignment, a de-sealing typology with no pedestrian shade component.
curation_reasons.2.15: Distinct system: no carriageway, so vegetation occupies the full width as primary infrastructure, giving canopy geometry and receptor exposure unlike any trafficked street.
curation_reasons.2.16: Distinct constrained system: high aspect ratio, little ground connection, cooling delivered mainly through vertical greening and permeable resurfacing rather than canopy.
curation_reasons.2.17: Distinct modular retrofit of the parking bay: intermittent tree islands and bioretention pockets that de-seal carriageway edge while retaining parking. Not a continuous strip.
curation_reasons.3.1: Document names it a clearly defined public-space typology: canopy organises the whole square. Distinct spatial structure and strong direct shade benefit.
curation_reasons.3.2: Document names it a valid public-space typology; combination of tree canopy, vegetated overhead structures and water-sensitive planting is a recognisable heat-refuge configuration.
curation_reasons.3.3: Document names it a valid typology; defined by de-sealing and infiltration rather than shade, so its cooling behaviour is genuinely distinct from tree and cooling plazas.
curation_reasons.3.4: Document names it a valid typology; replacing a hard civic surface with a substantial green ground plane is a distinct form with distinct cooling behaviour.
curation_reasons.3.5: Distinct enclosed-geometry system with restricted air movement and high radiant load; already an approved v1.1 typology (courtyard_greening).
curation_reasons.3.15: Same physical system as schoolyard greening — de-sealed, shaded, vegetated play landscape; differs only in institutional setting. Becomes canonical if 3.6 is dropped as a context.

curation_reasons.4.2: Size/service-area tier with distinct extent and vegetation share; supports a measurable park cool-island beyond a pocket park.
curation_reasons.4.4: Size tier large enough for multiple habitat types and documented influence on surrounding microclimate; distinct from neighbourhood scale.
curation_reasons.4.5: Top tier of the size axis; distinct behaviour through cool-air-mass generation and regional connectivity rather than site-scale shading.
curation_reasons.4.11: Permanent water bodies form the dominant substrate, giving evaporative cooling absent from vegetation-only parks; document's ecological reading, not the aquatic facility.
curation_reasons.4.15: Distinct form of multi-layer spontaneous vegetation, meadow and successional woodland replacing mown lawn; canonical entry for biodiversity and restoration parks.
curation_reasons.4.17: Canonical detention-landscape park; runoff storage and treatment give a distinct intermittent-moisture cooling regime, unlike a permanent water park.
curation_reasons.4.20: Distinct elongated form that distributes cooling along the urban fabric and aids ventilation; a park typology, not the tool's blue_green_corridor.
curation_reasons.4.22: Distinct dune, mangrove and shoreline form with context-gated availability; cooling regime governed by sea breeze and saline substrates.

curation_reasons.5.3: CREATION: canonical small dense woodland patch; high planting density on a constrained site gives rapid, spatially local canopy cooling.
curation_reasons.5.10: RESTORATION: canonical intervention on existing woodland, gated on woodland already being present; distinct from establishing new woodland.
curation_reasons.5.15: CREATION: canonical establishment of woodland on land not recently forested; availability gated on non-forested, ecologically suitable land.
curation_reasons.5.16: RESTORATION: re-establishment on previously forested land, gated on land history and residual seed bank; distinct from afforestation on that gate alone.
curation_reasons.5.18: CREATION: distinct linear belt sited between heat-generating and sensitive land uses; buffering and screening behaviour differs from patch woodland.
curation_reasons.6.1: Engineered wetland with distinct physical form and strong evaporative cooling; the rules name it explicitly as a valid composite typology.
curation_reasons.6.2: Constructed permanent water body with littoral planting; distinct from detention basin by permanent pool and continuous evaporative cooling.
curation_reasons.6.3: Constructed dry basin, distinct form; but document notes cooling is episodic and biodiversity limited, so cooling relevance is marginal.
curation_reasons.6.4: Distinct dual-function hard public space with terraced storage; document notes limited ecological value unless heavily vegetated, echoing the blue-roof caveat.
curation_reasons.6.5: Distinct hydrological intervention (culvert removal) creating new surface water plus riparian vegetation; not a restoration of an existing open channel.
curation_reasons.6.7: Canonical watercourse-restoration typology; distinct physical works on an existing open channel and its banks, with clear cooling behaviour.
curation_reasons.6.8: Distinct from river restoration: engineered vertical-walled waterway restored via edge planting, floating wetlands and habitat shelves rather than morphology.
curation_reasons.6.10: Distinct lateral intervention (levee setback, regrading, secondary channels) on the floodplain rather than the channel; large area, high cooling potential.
curation_reasons.6.11: Distinct still-water restoration (shoreline naturalisation, habitat islands, sediment management); large permanent water surface gives strong evaporative cooling.
curation_reasons.6.12: Distinct soft bank-protection system replacing hard engineering; document states it maintains natural coastal OR freshwater processes, so lake shores qualify alongside sea.
curation_reasons.6.13: Discrete built planted platform deployable where shoreline restoration is impossible; distinct form from constructed wetland, needs an existing water body of depth.
curation_reasons.6.14: Discrete vegetated strip beside a watercourse; document distinguishes it from riparian forest (5.6) by allowing grass, shrub or mixed vegetation.
curation_reasons.S12A.1: Shipped as Subsurface-flow treatment wetland. The flow is beneath a gravel bed, so there is no exposed water surface: inheriting the constructed-wetland class on the strength of the word wetland would attribute evaporative cooling to water that is under stone.
curation_reasons.S17.4: Woody vegetation restored on a tidal margin, cooling by shade and evapotranspiration. curation_reasons.S17.6: Native dune vegetation and sand management: a distinct coastal landform system. Deliberately not merged into the coastal park, which is a park and reports established-park values a restored dune does not earn.
curation_reasons.S17.7: Tidal and brackish wetland: emergent vegetation standing in shallow water, not open water. The large-water-body class was considered and rejected for the reason the two water archetypes are kept apart at all.
curation_reasons.7.1: Multifunctional terrestrial linear system named in the rules as a valid composite; distributes cooling and mobility through the urban fabric.
curation_reasons.7.2: Canonical habitat-driven corridor: low disturbance, species-appropriate vegetation, limited public access — physically distinct from the public-realm green corridor.
curation_reasons.7.4: Distinct combined terrestrial-aquatic linear system; already a literature-grounded v1.1 tool typology, so it is the canonical aquatic-medium corridor.
curation_reasons.7.5: Distinct from blue-green corridor: organised around an existing river with lateral bank-floodplain connection; strong cooling and ventilation potential.
curation_reasons.7.6: Distinct physical context (embankments, trackside pioneer and brownfield habitat, operational constraints); depends on an existing active or former rail alignment.
curation_reasons.7.14: Distinct physical form (dunes, mangroves, coastal wetlands, estuarine habitat) and distinct coastal cooling and erosion-resilience behaviour.
curation_reasons.8.1: Canonical productive-garden composite: beds, fruit trees, composting and water harvesting form one coherent, distinctly cooling planted system.
curation_reasons.8.2: Distinct plot-subdivided form with sheds and boundary hedges, but the document lists it as a governance model rather than a physical typology.
curation_reasons.8.3: Fruit- and nut-tree stand with flowering understory is a distinct physical form combining canopy shade with production.
curation_reasons.8.4: Multi-layered woodland-mimicking structure gives it a physical form and cooling behaviour distinct from orchards and gardens.
curation_reasons.8.5: Canonical field-scale production site; larger cultivated ground plane and infrastructure distinguish it physically from garden-scale entries.
curation_reasons.8.9: Document says productive function warrants separate identification, but it overlaps the tool's existing schoolyard_greening typology.
curation_reasons.8.15: Deliberate tree-plus-crop structure is a distinct physical form pairing canopy shade with cultivated ground; the canonical productive tree system.
curation_reasons.9.29: No individual counterpart; a distinct building open-space element with substantial permanent planting, not merely D5 or D6 planters.
curation_reasons.9.30: No individual counterpart; larger multi-layer planted terrace treated by the document as its own building open-space typology.
curation_reasons.9.33: No individual counterpart; landscape over podium or parking structure with pedestrian-level, semi-public cooling unlike any roof entry.
curation_reasons.S9.19: A recessed planted outdoor room with restricted air movement and high radiant load from the surrounding fabric: the enclosed-courtyard geometry at building scale. No counterpart in the catalogue, and distinguished by the source from both balcony and terrace.

curation_reasons.10.1: Document classes it as an infrastructure network, but it functions as the umbrella over 10.2-10.4; author may prefer only the specific networks.
curation_reasons.10.2: Water storage and movement give it a spatial structure and cooling behaviour distinct from a vegetation-only network.
curation_reasons.10.3: Connected shaded routes and thermal refuges prioritised by heat exposure form a distinct district-scale spatial system; the core district entry for this tool.
curation_reasons.10.4: Distinct substrate of walking, cycling and transit corridors, but its components and cooling behaviour overlap 10.3 substantially.
curation_reasons.10.10: Continuous district-wide canopy is a distinct physical structure with the strongest cooling, but it depends on the pending urban_forest ambiguity ruling.
curation_reasons.SA16: The deliberate removal of sealed surface to expose soil. Called an enabling intervention by the source, but unlike the soil operations of section 19 the intervention is itself the change of surface, and the permeable plaza was kept on the same de-sealing logic.
curation_reasons.S11B.16: Stepped terraces that change the landform rather than merely its cover: a distinct construction with its own water-retention behaviour, and the only slope entry that alters gradient rather than reinforcing it.
curation_reasons.S11B.17: The canonical vegetated slope: native vegetation and soil rehabilitation instead of conventional hard engineering. The catalogue had no slope entry of any kind, and embankments, cuttings and landslide scars are ordinary urban conditions.
curation_reasons.S19.4: The only entry in the section whose mechanism is the planting: it uses living vegetation as the primary remediation mechanism. It also answers a planning case the catalogue could not, the contaminated site.
curation_reasons.S21.8: Managed natural colonisation of a former industrial site, where the intervention is largely the decision not to intervene. There is no catalogue equivalent, the naturalistic park being a park, and the archetype's genuine zero floor suits a site in its first seasons.
